items.title: Reliable attached-client baseline
acceptance: Run pinned tmux and freshly built zz with isolated homes/config roots and short sockets; record binary hashes, source revision and dirty state, OS, TERM, shell and dimensions.

Retain attach, input, daemon and outer-screen diagnostics on every geometry-fixture timeout, proven by a driven failure. The geometry-report timeout recorded on macOS on 2026-09-09 is handed to TUI-013 for reproduction or explanation there (clause split 2026-09-09 by fabrico's deferral; reversible).

Produce a repeatable baseline at 80x24, 100x24 and 120x24 with all measured differences and fixture limitations retained, including the waived wide-terminal columns. This package proves fixture reliability, not runtime parity.
items.evidence_note: MEASURED 2026-09-09 on alienware (CachyOS, 16 cores, Linux) from worktree /home/demfabris/dev/zz-tui-lane at 576b6b745821856d9c00b3a62d6a1982fd8571e1, clean apart from this attempt's own files. zz built fresh in that worktree; pinned tmux d77c9dc6, sha256 df2cafcb212e8b69677dd57c2bd0c3bb59592eaf385d974ec0124526d6b63ee5, tmux -V next-3.8. TERM=xterm-ghostty, bash 5.3.15, LANG=en_US.UTF-8 with LC_TIME=pt_BR.UTF-8. environment.txt records both binaries' sha256, the worktree revision and dirty state, the OS, TERM, shell, locale and the sizes each fixture drives. The zz hash identifies the artifact but does not attest it: a cargo debug build of zz is not bit-reproducible on this box, and the cycle-18 reviewer rebuilt -p zz at this same worktree path from the same source and got a different hash, and a third from another worktree. Provenance rests on reproduction instead, which is stronger: that independently built zz reproduced these fixture results and TUI-002's 195 capture files byte for byte. The pin's hash verifies exactly. GEOMETRY: compat/tui-pane-geometry.sh exits 0 SIX times out of six, 4 to 5 seconds a run against its own 10 second bound - three runs of the fixture as it stands at origin/main and three of the fixture after this attempt's timeout-diagnostics change. 80x24 both 80 columns, 100x24 both 100, rows 23 on both sides at all three sizes. CLAUSE 2 IS NOT SATISFIED BY THIS ATTEMPT: the recorded macOS geometry-report timeout is neither reproduced nor explained here, and it stays open. The stale-pre-fix-binary story this attempt first argued is REFUTED by the campaign's own registry, inside the very gap that was cited as its authority. tui.client-input-backpressure (closed 2026-09-07 at 0bed7fe7) does cite compat/tui-pane-geometry.sh among its evidence and does record the cause exactly, crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs flush_output blocking the main event loop; but its resolution rules that stall out as the cause of a macOS geometry expiry, verbatim: "It also exited 0 at origin/main 012b4dcc before the fix, so the macbook expiry the cycle-17 gate recorded is not this stall reproducing there: that script drives the pane through the CLI's send-keys, not through the client's stdin, and its inner clients run inside an outer pinned tmux that reads their output continuously, so no backpressure ever builds. What remains on the macbook is unexplained and belongs to whoever next runs the tool there." Two refutations, either one sufficient. EMPIRICAL: 012b4dcc is 2026-09-07T10:45:51-03:00, after the fixture reached its current shape at 314c55e0 (00:15:42) and before the fix at 0bed7fe7 (13:31:08), which is exactly the window a stale binary would have to come from, and the registry records this fixture exiting 0 there - so a pre-fix binary running this fixture is measured as PASSING. MECHANISM, and it is platform-independent: the fixture's inner clients run inside an outer pinned tmux that drains their output continuously, so the backpressure flush_output stalled on never builds in this fixture at all; if no backpressure builds, the macOS pty write buffer's size is irrelevant and the pre-fix stall cannot fire on any platform, which the earlier draft's pty-buffer hedge does not reach. WHAT SURVIVES of that explanation is two measurements, neither of which reaches the macOS record: the fixture and the runtime are sound at this revision (six exit-0 runs, the measure() wait nowhere near its bound), and the named backpressure cause is measurably absent here (compat/run.sh --strict-geometry smoke/tui-client-input-backpressure exits 0 with 0 divergences). CLOSING CLAUSE 2 NEEDS a run of compat/tui-pane-geometry.sh on macOS with an attested binary, retaining the timeout dump this attempt added if the geometry-report wait fires. The timed-out binary's own revision is unrecoverable: the shared checkout's target/debug/zz was rebuilt on this box at 18:25 on 2026-09-09, so its hash says nothing about the record. FIXTURE CHANGE, in zone: a bounded wait that runs out now copies out, before the scratch tree is removed, which wait fired, both outer screens via capture-pane -p -e -S -, both servers' client and pane lists, the zz daemon's stdout and stderr, and each attached client's own stderr teed out of its pane; the fixture also pins ZZ_LOG_DIR into its scratch tree and scrubs XDG_STATE_HOME so it can no longer write into the box's real state directory. Proved by sabotage: file_has_two_fields was made to demand three fields, the fixture exited 2 with the record's own text "zz geometry report did not happen within 10 seconds" and left fourteen files, retained under timeout-diagnostics/; the edit was reverted and runs 4 to 6 are the unsabotaged fixture. That dump is what a macOS run would need to retain, and it is the part of this attempt clause 2 can still use. CLAUSE 3 RECORD, for TUI-004: at 120x24 the pin hands its pane 120 columns and zz hands its pane 91, rows 23 on both. The 29 column difference is the sidebar's 28 plus its 1 column border, the same arithmetic as AUTO_HIDE_COLUMNS = 80 + 28 + 1 = 109 in crates/zz-tui/src/sidebar.rs. Recorded, not asserted: tui.sidebar-auto-hide is a standing decision and TUI-004 owns changing it. FIXTURE LIMITATION AND A NEW DIVERGENCE: compat/status-row.sh exits 1 on this box, 2 of 11 comparisons, and the cause is the locale rather than the status row. Only the two steps that still carry the default status-right differ, and only in %b: the pin prints "09-set-26" and zz prints "09-Sep-26". The pin expands %b through libc strftime(3), which honours LC_TIME=pt_BR.UTF-8; zz expands it in crates/zz-mux/src/formats.rs:4707 format_datetime through chrono StrftimeItems and format_with_items, which is locale-independent and always English. Control run settles it: LC_ALL=C LC_TIME=C, same fixture, same binaries, exit 0, all 11 identical. The fixture is untouched by this branch, so it is red at origin/main on this box too and the red is not this lane's. No gap in compat/tmux-gaps.json records it, so it needs a registry owner; the fix would land in crates/zz-mux, which this cycle's wire rule puts out of reach, so it is measured and left. It is also a limitation of status-row.sh as a baseline: the fixture pins the pane title but not LC_TIME, so its default-row comparison carries the caller's locale; pinning the locale would hide the divergence rather than record it. OTHER PROOFS AT THIS TIP: compat/attached-client.sh exits 0, "attached-client compatibility: PASS". GATE, cycle 1, 2026-09-09 at 5dd932abb93c2e88f3190be42afeeed00ece6368 in /home/demfabris/dev/zz-gate-fixtures: every proof command above re-run at the merged tip on a zz this gate built itself, sha256 ddc5ae0f7be9e52b55dac82a8285c50f74a9684236986d277f54e1d8aa3b3254. Three geometry runs exit 0 at 4.8s, 4.5s and 4.7s, output byte-identical to all six committed runs; attached-client PASS; the backpressure scenario exit 0; tracker_test, both tracker checks and compat/check.sh exit 0. status-row.sh exits 1 exactly as recorded, %b only, and exits 0 under the LC_ALL=C control; the branch touches neither that fixture nor any crate source, so that red is origin/main's on this box and it is retained here as clause 3's fixture limitation. STATUS STAYS ACTIVE: clause 2 is open and cannot be closed on this box, because the recorded timeout happened on macOS and this box is Linux. The proof block recorded here stands for CLAUSES 1 AND 3 ONLY and is not a claim about clause 2. The reviewer's one confirmed defect was a nit addressed to the gate rather than to the branch - record the hash of the zz the gate builds, not environment.txt's 3cb6e284 - and it is done: ddc5ae0f7be9e52b55dac82a8285c50f74a9684236986d277f54e1d8aa3b3254 is a fourth distinct hash for source identical to origin/main, which settles that a debug build of zz is not reproducible here and that provenance rests on reproduction. SPLIT 2026-09-09: fabrico deferred the macOS reproduction (no macbook access now; the campaign continues on Linux) and the macOS half of clause 2 moved to TUI-013, added scope, so the baseline number never counts it as quietly done. What this obligation claims under the amended clause 2 is exactly what its proof block already records: the fixture retains the full timeout dump, proven by sabotage (fourteen files under timeout-diagnostics/), and the recorded macOS expiry is neither reproduced nor explained HERE - that work is TUI-013's, opening on this attempt's refutation of the stale-binary story and the retention machinery. decided 2026-09-09 by fabrico, relayed in-session to the orchestrator ('can we continue for now and record that test for later'); reversible - reopening TUI-001 and folding TUI-013 back undoes it.
items.next_action: None here: verified under the amended clause 2. The macOS reproduction or explanation is TUI-013; compat/tui/run-2.js is its ready-to-launch runner.

items.title: Complete screen and interaction comparison
acceptance: Reuse existing attached-client drivers to compare all decoded cells, glyph widths, styles, cursor position/visibility/shape, geometry and resulting interaction state at named settled checkpoints.
Demonstrate that independent glyph, color/attribute, cursor and geometry changes fail with a useful location/state difference. Equivalent raw escape spellings must not fail.

Retain captures and environment at 80, 100, 109 and 120 columns, including small heights, split/zoom/resize and status off/on/multiple rows/top/bottom. Declare each controlled dynamic value and comparison rule.
items.evidence_note: MEASURED 2026-09-09 on alienware by the new fixture compat/tui-screen-diff.sh, which compares EVERY decoded cell of both screens plus the cursor at named settled checkpoints, both binaries attached inside one outer pinned tmux. zz sha256 3cb6e28437cd028b49c2c2eb07c4414a69226518bf2f287e7c52123d5bf70a38 at 576b6b74; pin d77c9dc6 sha256 df2cafcb212e8b69677dd57c2bd0c3bb59592eaf385d974ec0124526d6b63ee5. RESULT: 33 asserted checkpoints identical, 32 recorded, 65 recorded cursor differences; exit 0 twice in a row, and run 2's 195 capture files are byte-identical to run 1's. Asserted means every row of the outer pane matched byte for byte with its escapes and the asserted cursor tuple matched, at 80x24, 100x24 and 80x10, across fresh attach, status off, status on, split-window -v, resize-pane -Z, unzoom, an outer resize away and back, status 2, status-position top, and a row of CJK, combining and emoji glyphs. Not one cell differed. Two results beyond the count: the small height 80x10 behaves exactly like the wide sizes, and resizing the 120-column client down to 100 makes the two screens identical again cell for cell, so the sidebar is the whole of the 109-and-above difference and hiding it leaves nothing behind. CLAUSE 2, the demonstration: --self-check exits 0 only when four sabotages are each caught in their own channel and three equivalences are reported nowhere. glyph (one character of OUTPUT, from a file each side reads under its own HOME so the typed command is identical bytes) -> rows differ; colour (status-style bg=red on one side) -> rows differ; cursor (an unterminated line of a different length) -> the CURSOR tuple differs; geometry (split-window on one side) -> rows differ; and attribute order in a style, bg=red against bg=colour1, and \033[1mBOLD\033[0m against \033[01mBOLD\033[m -> nothing differs. Two of these were rebuilt after the first attempt measured something other than what it claimed. colour.c colour_fromstring gives red the value 1 and colour1 the value 1|COLOUR_FLAG_256, two DIFFERENT values, and yet both reach the outer grid as the same cell and capture-pane -e re-emits both as \e[41m, so the pair really does collapse: the fixture states the measurement, not the header-file reading. The first cursor sabotage sent a marker afterwards, which put the cursor back at a fresh prompt on both sides and reported no cursor difference at all; it now settles on a substring the two sides' own sabotage output share. CLAUSE 3, the covered subset: 80, 100, 109 and 120 columns, a small height at 80x10, split, zoom and resize, and status off, on, two rows, top and bottom are all driven, with all 195 captures and both cursor tuples retained. Every controlled dynamic value is declared in the fixture header with its rule: status-right '' (the clock, and the %d-%b-%y locale divergence TUI-001 recorded), status-left L, automatic-rename off plus rename-window win, select-pane -T (the recorded pane.runtime-facts decision), and an inner shell of ENV= PS1='$ ' exec /bin/sh handed to new-session and split-window. Global options are reset to each server's defaults before every attach so a case cannot leak into the next. WHAT REMAINS, and the one judgement the reviewer should make: all three clauses have evidence on this branch, so this is review, but ONE channel is compared and printed without being gated. Clause 1 asks for the cursor's SHAPE to be COMPARED and it is, on both sides at all 65 checkpoints, with both values printed every run; it is not asserted, because zz and the pin genuinely differ there today, and a sabotage of that channel could not be told apart from the standing divergence. A shape regression would therefore not turn this fixture red. If the reviewer reads clause 1 as requiring a gate rather than a comparison, downgrade this to active on that point alone; nothing else in the three clauses is short. THREE NEW DIVERGENCES, none with a registry owner, all recorded with both sides' bytes printed on every run. (a) CURSOR ATTRIBUTES, at 65 of 65 checkpoints: the pin reports shape=default blinking=0 colour=none and zz reports shape=block blinking=1 colour=#e5c07b, because crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs:1770-1799 writes DECSCUSR and an OSC 12 cursor colour on every cursor placement while the pin writes neither. Cursor position and visibility ARE asserted and match everywhere. (b) COLOUR CLASSES in the pane body: the same three cells written as named, indexed and RGB come back from the pin as \e[31m, \e[38;5;196m and \e[38;2;1;2;3m, and from zz as \e[38;2;205;0;0m, \e[38;2;255;0;0m and \e[38;2;1;2;3m. zz resolves the named and the indexed cell through its palette and hands the terminal RGB. tui.status-row's closed class-1 finding fixed the STATUS ROW; the pane body still promotes. (c) DEFAULT FOREGROUND: with status-style bg=colour4 and no foreground named, the pin emits no foreground and zz emits an explicit RGB 216,222,233. Under the default status-style the two agree byte for byte, which is why compat/status-row.sh never saw it. None of the three is fixable inside this cycle's zones: (a) is in crates/zz-tui/src outside TUI-001's excursion, and (b) and (c) reach the daemon's frame representation. Also not covered by this attempt: mouse, focus and bracketed paste (TUI-008), copy mode and search overlays (TUI-005), pane-border-status (TUI-004), more than one window, and a second attached client. THE SETTLE, measured not assumed: the marker alone was not enough. Two runs disagreed at the 80x24 zoom checkpoint, zz row 11 holding '$' in one and nothing in the next, because the shell writes the marker line and the prompt that follows it as two separate writes and a capture can land between them. A checkpoint is now settled when its marker is on the screen AND the screen has not changed between two polls; three consecutive runs after that fix were exit 0 with byte-identical captures. No wait in the fixture is a sleep. The timeout dump earned its place before it was sabotaged: the first full run timed out at 109x24 and the retained screen showed in one line that zz draws its sidebar to the LEFT of the pane there, so the marker shared its row with sidebar cells and a whole-line match could never succeed - a fixture fault, fixed by matching the marker as a substring. GATE, cycle 1, 2026-09-09 at 5dd932abb93c2e88f3190be42afeeed00ece6368: all three clauses re-proved at the merged tip on a zz this gate built itself, sha256 ddc5ae0f7be9e52b55dac82a8285c50f74a9684236986d277f54e1d8aa3b3254 - a THIRD independent binary after the worker's and the reviewer's. tui-screen-diff.sh exit 0 in 57.3s with the same summary line, and its 195 capture files plus its 29242-byte stdout are byte-identical to the committed evidence (diff -r exit 0, zero bytes); --self-check exit 0 in 24.1s with stdout byte-identical to the committed self-check.stdout.txt; attached-client PASS; both trackers and compat/check.sh exit 0. Nothing any fixture reported contradicts this obligation. STATUS STAYS REVIEW RATHER THAN VERIFIED, and the reason is the ledger's own rule, not a doubt about the evidence: compat/tui/tracker.py requires every dependency of a verified obligation to be verified too, and this obligation depends on TUI-001, which stays active on its open clause 2, so setting verified here would make tracker.py check fail. The proof block is recorded anyway: the cycle that closes TUI-001 clause 2 on macOS can flip this to verified on these measurements without re-running them. The reviewer confirmed no defect on this obligation. VERIFIED 2026-09-09: TUI-001 reached verified when its macOS clause split to TUI-013 (fabrico's deferral, recorded there), which satisfies the dependency rule; per this note's own provision the banked, thrice-reproduced measurements flip this obligation without re-running them. No new measurement was taken for this flip.
items.next_action: Done. The three recorded divergences still need registry owners (cursor attributes from crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs:1770-1799, named and indexed colours promoted to RGB in the pane body, and the explicit default foreground); the recorded half of the cursor tuple starts asserting the moment the first of those closes. TUI-003, TUI-004 and TUI-010 are now ready.

items.title: Stock launcher, command and key behavior
acceptance: With clean config roots, compare bare packaged launch, attach and new-session on empty/live servers plus new-window and split-window. Assert stdout/stderr/exits, selected targets, pane kinds and the complete attached screen.
Drive unmodified stock split, chooser, rename, selection, zoom and detach bindings through actual stdin. Direct split-window creating a terminal does not substitute for testing its stock binding.

Test root bindings and application keys overlapping Ctrl-\ and Alt-s/Alt-S. Chrome cannot consume them outside its owning context. Exercise explicit config roots, -f and existing zz layering separately and record any policy conflict.
items.evidence_note: Source inspection found bare launcher new-session -A, stock bindings using native picker/sidebar commands, and chrome shortcuts before daemon routing. Explicit split-window already creates terminals. Accepted default-key decisions do not establish the new contract.
items.next_action: Capture unmodified tmux and zz launch/key behavior, then separate shared command/key policy from client presentation without adding a compatibility profile.

items.title: Default canvas, status and pane borders
acceptance: Ordinary tmux commands preserve the pinned canvas at narrow and wide dimensions; width never invokes the sidebar. Cover split, zoom, pane-border-status, small heights and resize restoration.
Compare full status/border presentation for default/custom formats, top/bottom/off/multiple rows, named/indexed/RGB colors, theme options and terminal light/dark reports.
Compare copy/view/prefix indicators and message/prompt restoration without waiving cells occupied by zz hints. Turn the three recorded theme differences into asserted comparisons.
items.evidence_note: CYCLE 3, THE SIDEBAR DECISION, LANDED AND PROVED. PRODUCT DECISION: terminal width never invokes the sidebar; it is client-local chrome that appears only through focus-sidebar or a user binding, so at every width a terminal client's canvas is the one pinned tmux draws. decided 2026-09-09 by the orchestrator under fabrico's TUI parity contract of 2026-09-09; reversible. OLD BEHAVIOUR: crates/zz-tui/src/sidebar.rs AUTO_HIDE_COLUMNS = 80 + 28 + 1 = 109 with a three-state Visibility enum whose Auto arm showed the sidebar from 109 columns. MEASURED PIN BEHAVIOUR: the pin adds no column of chrome at any width, which is why tui-pane-geometry.sh recorded its 120-column columns and tui-screen-diff.sh recorded its 109 and 120 sizes instead of asserting them. NEW STANCE: State carries one `shown` flag defaulting to false and visible() is `shown && columns >= MIN_MANUAL_COLUMNS`, so 50 columns is only the floor below which the command declines. The TUI portion of tui.sidebar-auto-hide is updated with the same decision and the GUI scope retained. MEASURED AT THE FIX: tui-pane-geometry.sh asserts columns at 80, 100 and 120 and exits 0 (120 both 120, rows 23 both sides); its record mode is deleted because no size needs it. tui-screen-diff.sh promotes 109 and 120 from record to same, moves its resize cases across the retired threshold in both directions, and reports 58 asserted checkpoints identical with 15 recorded. THE COMMAND AND ITS WITHDRAWAL: a new 120x24-sidebar case binds F8 to focus-sidebar on the zz side only, requires the zz screen to DIFFER from the pin's while the sidebar is up, then sends q on the sidebar key table and requires the two screens to be identical again; the same first half is a --self-check sabotage. A one-shot `zz focus-sidebar` cannot drive it, the daemon answers 'focus-sidebar requires an interactive client'. FOUND WHILE PROVING THIS, RECORDED NOT FIXED: with the sidebar gone the status ROW is the only place status-left can land, and a STYLED status-left longer than status-left-length leaves the row entirely on zz. display-message -p '#{T;=/#{status-left-length}:status-left}' with status-left '#[fg=red,bold]LEFT' answers '#[fg=red,bold]LEFT' on the pin and '#[fg=red,b' on zz, and a styled status-right loses ten characters the same way; format.c format_trim_left copies a #[...] section through without counting it while crates/zz-mux/src/formats.rs truncate_value counts every printable byte and cuts the marker in half, so the unterminated marker takes the whole band off the row. tui-screen-diff.sh records it at every size as styled-left-trim, and crates/zz/tests/cli_binary.rs attached_tui_renders_daemon_authored_styled_status_labels now raises status-left-length past the marker so it asserts what it means to assert; it used to pass only because the sidebar drew the styled label. The fix is in the format engine's trim, crates/zz-mux, which this lane does not own. CYCLE 3, THE CURSOR ATTRIBUTES, FIXED FOR THE PIN'S DEFAULT AND THE RESIDUE RECORDED. OLD BEHAVIOUR: crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs place_viewport_cursor turned every cursor placement into `\x1b[<n> q` plus `\x1b]12;#rrggbb\x07`, and the three chrome cursors (command-output search, sidebar editor, status message) each wrote `\x1b[6 q`, so the outer tmux reported shape=block blinking=1 colour=#e5c07b for zz against shape=default blinking=0 colour=none for the pin, at every size and every checkpoint. MEASURED PIN BEHAVIOUR, read out of tty.c tty_update_cursor rather than guessed: with the pane's screen at SCREEN_CURSOR_DEFAULT the pin emits Se only if it had previously changed the style, and tty_force_cursor_colour with ccolour -1 emits nothing at all, so a pane whose application never asked leaves the outer terminal's own cursor exactly as it found it. NEW STANCE: the raw TUI writes neither DECSCUSR nor OSC 12; it keeps \x1b[?25h and \x1b[?25l, which are the pin's cnorm and civis. MEASURED AT THE FIX: tui-screen-diff.sh folds shape, blink, very-visible and colour into CURSOR_ASSERTED_FORMAT and drops the recorded half entirely; 58 asserted checkpoints identical with the whole tuple asserted, where the same run previously printed 73 recorded cursor differences. --self-check gains 'cursor shape, DECSCUSR on one side', which plants \033[5 q in one side's file, has both sides type the same command, and requires the difference to be reported in the CURSOR channel. THE COVERED SUBSET, AND WHAT REMAINS: covered is every cursor the campaign can drive with a pane whose application never asks for a style, which is every checkpoint of every size plus the sidebar case. NOT covered, and recorded at every size as cursor-style-request: a pane that DOES ask. The pin tracks s->cstyle and s->ccolour per screen and forwards the request; zz cannot, and this is a wire finding, not a render one. libghostty's render state has no 'the application has not asked' value - RenderStateCursorVisualStyle is BAR, BLOCK, UNDERLINE or BLOCK_HOLLOW - and zz_terminal::Cursor packs those same four into two bits with no default arm, so crates/zz-terminal/src/session.rs substitutes Block/false/foreground for a pane that never asked and the client cannot tell the two apart. The field it would need: a cursor-style-requested and cursor-colour-requested pair beside the packed Cursor, fed from libghostty's COLOR_CURSOR_HAS_VALUE and from style tracking zz-terminal does not keep yet. Out of this lane's zones; left with the measurement. CYCLE 3, THE CANVAS MATRIX. compat/tui-screen-diff.sh now drives six sizes (80x24, 100x24, 80x10, 80x6, 109x24, 120x24) and 111 asserted checkpoints, all identical, plus 42 recorded. What the matrix gained: PANE BORDERS, pane-border-status top, bottom and off with two panes on the screen and every pane's title pinned; A SMALLER HEIGHT, 80x6, where the status block, a split and a pane status row all compete for six rows; RESIZE ACROSS THE RETIRED THRESHOLD, 80 out to 120 and back, 109 to 120, 120 down to 100, all asserted; COLOUR CLASSES ON THE STATUS ROW, status-style with a named, an indexed and an RGB pair and a window-status-current-format carrying one of each, all asserted identical, which is the closed presentation:tui-status-row-colour-encoding holding under a whole-screen comparison rather than a one-row one; THE SERVER THEME OPTION, recorded. PANE BORDERS ARE THE ONE SPLIT ASSERTION. Measured 2026-09-09: the border text and the rows it costs are the pin's cell for cell, and the border COLOUR is not - the pin draws an active border as \\e[38;2;154;205;50m, pane-active-border-style fg=themegreen through the dark theme's yellowgreen, and the raw TUI draws \\e[38;2;77;163;235m\\e[48;2;16;19;24m, its own blue over an explicit background where the pin leaves the ground default. Neither half is this lane's to flip: the theme colour sits inside the recorded presentation:tui-status-row-theme-defaults decision, whose scope keeps zz's theme for every TUI surface other than the status row, and the explicit ground is the same class as the standing default-fg record. So the fixture gained a `text` mode: every glyph, every column and the cursor ASSERTED, the styles recorded with that reason. --self-check gains three cases for it - the plain comparison catches a glyph difference, stays silent on a pure colour difference, and the styled comparison still catches that same colour - so the mode cannot quietly assert nothing. THE TERMINAL LIGHT/DARK REPORT IS NOT A CHANNEL THIS FIXTURE CAN DRIVE, measured rather than skipped: #{client_theme} answers empty on both binaries from a one-shot client, and with a client attached the report is the OUTER terminal's own answer to OSC 11, which is the box's and not the fixture's. What can be driven is the forced server option, and `set -s theme light` is recorded at every size as theme-light: the pin re-resolves the ten theme colours per client from it and zz cannot read the option at all. CYCLE 3, THE THEME ARM: MEASURED, NOT LANDED, AND THE RECORDED SHAPE IS CORRECTED. The roster is 21 names, not the eleven the cycle-18 handoff recorded - `theme` plus TEN dark-theme-* AND TEN light-theme-*, because server_client_update_theme_colours (server-client.c:1173) picks the dark or the light set per client - so TMUX_OPTION_CONSUMERS goes 118 to 139, not to 129, and the count is hard-coded in two places. ON A THROWAWAY BUILD WITH THE 21 NAMES ADDED zz answered exactly what the pin answers: #{E:dark-theme-green} green, #{E:dark-theme-black} black, #{theme} detect, and colour124 after `set -s dark-theme-green colour124`, where at this tip all four answer empty on zz. That also settles the daemon side: no new zz-mux accessor is needed, the resolver fits entirely in crates/zz-daemon/src/status.rs. WHY IT DID NOT LAND, and it is not a budget answer. (1) crates/zz-mux/src/compat_manifest_tests.rs enforces a PARTITION between the consumer roster and the option:<name> items tracked in compat/tmux-gaps.json: the two must be disjoint and must together equal the 180-name catalog. All 21 names are items of the OPEN gap options.theme-palette, which this lane does not own, so the consumer half alone forces closing 21 items of somebody else's gap - tracked count 62 to 41, scope counts [15,44,41,18] to [36,44,41,18] - and would assert that zz consumes options it still would not act on. The consumer half and the wire half are ONE landing, not two. (2) The transport is postcard, which is not self-describing, so the appended StatusLine field is not tolerated by an older decoder and PROTOCOL_VERSION 99 to 100 is mandatory; that version reaches clients/web, a separate cargo workspace with its own lockfile, and clients/ios and clients/macos through zz-client-ffi and include/zz-client.h, none of which this lane's proof set builds. A bump landed here could not be shown not to break them. PROTOCOL_VERSION STAYS 99 and the cycle's allowed bump is unspent. The field it would need, for whoever takes it with options.theme-palette in scope: StatusLine gains theme: [TmuxColour; 10] in colour_theme_table order - TmuxColour and not RGB, because the pin keeps the class it was given and colour124 has to leave as \\e[48;5;124m - defaulting to the pin's dark set so a client that has not had its first publication keeps today's behaviour, and crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs write_ground and resolve_tmux_colour re-dispatch on the published value instead of the hard-coded DARK_THEME_COLOURS names. The measurement is appended to tui.status-row's reason as a dated TUI measurement. STATUS: acceptance clauses 1 and 2 have whole-screen evidence at this tip. Clause 3 is OPEN: the copy, view and prefix indicators and the message and prompt restoration are not driven by any fixture yet, and the three recorded theme rows in compat/status-row.sh stay recorded because the wire half did not land.
items.next_action: Clause 3: drive the copy, view and prefix indicators and the message and prompt restoration through the whole-screen fixture, and take the theme arm as one landing with options.theme-palette in scope.

items.title: Pane copy mode and search
acceptance: Compare stock emacs and vi pane copy tables, forward/backward search editing, repeat search, numeric counts, line/page movement, selection, rectangles, copy and cancel through actual input.
Assert cells, mode/search prompts, cursor, selection styles and resulting paste-buffer bytes, including live mode/binding changes and return to terminal input.
Keep ordinary pane search proof separate from command-output search. Inventory remaining copy actions against their existing authority before claiming complete table coverage.
items.evidence_note: Command-output search editing works, but ordinary pane TerminalUiCommand search reports terminal search is unsupported here. Existing copy closures cover narrower contracts.
items.next_action: Reproduce stock forward/backward search in an ordinary pane, then identify existing proof for each pane-copy acceptance clause.

items.title: Chooser and command-output presentation
acceptance: Compare choose-tree, choose-buffer, find-window and long command output with stock bindings: screen extent, status retention, titles, rows, shortcuts, previews, tagging, filtering, help and scrolling.
Compare output search and prompt lifecycle without replacement zz-only bindings, including selection/copy and return to the underlying pane.
Retain behavioral coverage while replacing alternate zz/tmux marker expectations with whole-screen evidence for the claimed surfaces.
items.evidence_note: The renderer has custom chooser title/footer and output header/geometry. Existing attached checks use separate indicator expectations and one native search binding, so their navigation pass is not full presentation proof.
items.next_action: Capture default choose-tree and long command output on both clients; classify differences in layout, content, style and input.

items.title: Prompts, menus, popups and pane labels
acceptance: Compare command-prompt, confirm-before, display-menu, display-popup and display-panes placement, clipping/wrapping, title/style, cursor, configured keys and size changes.
Exercise nested surfaces/messages, keyboard and mouse cancellation/selection, restoration and no input delivery to covered panes.
Reuse existing behavioral closures as regressions and independently measure complete output at the final candidate.
items.evidence_note: Existing attached fixtures cover several overlay behaviors but do not claim whole-screen equality. Prompt placement currently depends on sidebar visibility.
items.next_action: Inventory existing overlay cases and add whole-screen checkpoints to a small prompt and popup case before broadening.

items.title: Mouse, paste, focus and key ownership
acceptance: Compare stock/custom root and copy mouse bindings, drag selection, border resize, status clicks, wheel and double/triple clicks with mouse on/off and application tracking.
Assert target, action, screen and no unintended input leakage across copy mode, prompts, choosers and popups. Cover paste, focus and supported repeat/release paths.
Reassess the TUI portion of accepted native-mouse decisions while preserving explicit zz bindings and other clients.
items.evidence_note: The registry accepts client-owned gestures instead of several stock mouse entries. Current input gates mux/application tracking, but the full interaction matrix has not been run.
items.next_action: Select one stock root mouse binding and one copy gesture, record delivery and reference effects, then expand the table.

items.title: Outer-terminal capabilities and fidelity
acceptance: Declare a finite capability matrix covering legacy/extended keys, user keys, paste, focus/mouse, color/theme replies, Unicode widths and alternate-screen restoration.
Compare effects and client facts for cells/styles and global flags including -2, -u and -T. Ignored flags and waived capability cases remain visible obligations.
Preserve named/indexed/RGB color behavior under palette changes while accepting equivalent escape spelling. Expand coverage through explicit cases rather than claiming every terminal.
items.evidence_note: The TUI reconstructs cells/styles and uses terminal-name capability checks. The CLI consumes several terminal flags without applying them. Accepted negotiation/engine decisions require bounded remeasurement.
items.next_action: Write the capability matrix from the pin and tty setup, starting with one controlled legacy and one extended-key terminal.

items.title: Slow output, recovery and client lifecycle
acceptance: Measure prolonged terminal backpressure past the writer budget, deliver an observable bound key while undrained, and verify bounded memory and response within a declared reference-derived deadline.
Resume reading and compare the final screen. Detach under backlog and prove no queued paint appears after terminal restoration.
Exercise different-sized simultaneous terminal clients, read-only attach, detach/reattach and supported transport recovery. Compare selected targets, geometry, focus and final screen.
items.evidence_note: The short-backlog stdin fix is closed. The open queue-budget gap records 4 MiB saturation where zz input waits for drain after prolonged backlog; this campaign has not remeasured it.
items.next_action: Reuse the registered prolonged-backpressure reproduction and record current reference/zz behavior before choosing an output recovery change.

items.title: Remaining stock client command inventory
acceptance: Enumerate existing stock-client exceptions, including choose-client, clock-mode, customize-mode, suspend/lock, refresh and capture/output, into a finite command/flag roster.
For each entry compare exact stdout/stderr/exits and attached state/screen. Declare binary-output and unsupported-platform cases without counting them as parity.
Add stable child obligations for independent uncovered commands and retain this parent until the declared roster is proved.
items.evidence_note: The previous campaign accepts several native client-tool and transport choices. Everyday terminal and selected query tests cannot establish this remaining inventory.
items.next_action: Extract the command roster from the linked gaps and pin inventory; split independent command families before implementation.

items.title: Superset commands beside tmux behavior
acceptance: Invoke existing sidebar, picker, browser, Agent and editor commands directly and through user bindings. No compatibility profile or feature activation flag is required.
Exercise create/select/split/resize/detach/reattach around those commands. Standard commands retain their meaning and input ownership; withdrawing extra UI restores the expected terminal canvas.
Verify client-local sidebar state across clients and browser capability/provider fallback. Retain existing Agent/editor cards; new feature development is outside this obligation.
items.evidence_note: Sidebar and picker work today; browser frames require Kitty support and a provider. Agent/editor show cards. These surfaces have no tmux visual counterpart; proof concerns their declared commands and surrounding terminal behavior.
items.next_action: Freeze existing superset command behavior and add composition cases after ordinary terminal and input contracts have passing proof.

items.title: Recorded macOS geometry-report timeout
acceptance: On macOS, build an attested zz (recorded revision, clean worktree) and run compat/tui-pane-geometry.sh against the pin three consecutive times; reproduce or explain the geometry-report timeout recorded on 2026-09-09 using the fixture's retained attach, input, daemon and outer-screen diagnostics. A timeout or missing report in this attempt fails it.

If the timeout does not reproduce, close on the bound the evidence supports: the original record was unattested and never rebuilt, its one proposed mechanism is refuted by tui.client-input-backpressure's resolution, and an attested build passes; name no unevidenced defect. If it reproduces, diagnose from the retained dump and hand any runtime fault to its owning obligation with the reproduction.
items.evidence_note: SPLIT FROM TUI-001 CLAUSE 2 on 2026-09-09 (decided 2026-09-09 by fabrico, relayed in-session: 'can we continue for now and record that test for later'; reversible). THE RECORD: an exploratory run on 2026-09-09 on the macbook exited 2 with 'zz geometry report did not happen within 10 seconds' from an unattested, never-rebuilt target/debug/zz whose revision is unrecoverable. ALREADY KNOWN: the stale-pre-fix-binary explanation is refuted twice by tui.client-input-backpressure's resolution (the fixture exited 0 at pre-fix 012b4dcc, and the outer pinned tmux drains continuously so the stalled backpressure can never build in this fixture on any platform); cycle 1 made compat/tui-pane-geometry.sh retain the full timeout dump on every expiry, proven by sabotage (see compat/tui/evidence/TUI-001/attempt-01/timeout-diagnostics/), so any macOS recurrence self-documents; an attested Linux build passes six of six runs in 4-5s against the 10s bound. WHAT THIS NEEDS: one attested build and three fixture runs on the macbook.
items.next_action: Whenever fabrico is next on the macbook: follow compat/tui/README.md 'Launching the deferred macOS run' (mint F-TUI-MACOS-TIMEOUT, launch compat/tui/run-2.js). Nothing blocks on this meanwhile.
